guidelines.title: button groups
guidelines.rule: Present related actions as a small cluster of buttons, aligned horizontally or vertically; split into more groups if there are more than three or four actions.

citation.source: Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Doing Things — Button Groups (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia)

pass_when: Related actions sit in one small horizontal or vertical cluster; more than three or four are split into further groups.
fail_when: Related actions are scattered, or more than three or four sit in one undifferentiated strip.

guidelines.title: hover or popup tools
guidelines.rule: Associate an object with tools that appear on hover or as a pop-up rather than crowding the main chrome.

citation.source: Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Doing Things — Hover or Pop-Up Tools (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia)

pass_when: Occasional object tools appear on hover or in a pop-up tied to the object; they are not stuffed into persistent chrome.
fail_when: Occasional tools occupy the main chrome and crowd it.

guidelines.title: action panel
guidelines.rule: Instead of burying a large set of related commands in menus, present them on a richly organized panel that stays visible.

citation.source: Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Doing Things — Action Panel (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia)

pass_when: A large related command set is on a visible, organized panel.
fail_when: That set exists only buried in menus, with no staying-visible panel.

guidelines.title: prominent done or assumed next
guidelines.rule: Place the control that finishes the transaction (or the assumed next step) at the end of the visual flow; make it prominent and well labeled.

citation.source: Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Doing Things — Prominent Done or Assumed Next Step (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia)

pass_when: Finish / assumed-next sits at the end of the visual flow, is prominent, and is well labeled.
fail_when: That control is weak, unlabeled, or not at the end of the flow.

guidelines.title: smart menu items
guidelines.rule: Change menu labels dynamically so they state precisely what the command will do when invoked.

citation.source: Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Doing Things — Smart Menu Items (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia)

pass_when: Menu labels reword with context to state the actual command.
fail_when: Labels stay generic/static and do not state what will happen.

guidelines.title: preview
guidelines.rule: Show a preview or summary of what will happen when the user performs the action.

citation.source: Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Doing Things — Preview (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia)

pass_when: A preview or summary of the result is available before the person commits.
fail_when: The action commits with no preview or summary of what will happen.

guidelines.title: cancelability
guidelines.rule: Provide a way to instantly cancel a time-consuming operation with no side effects.

citation.source: Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Doing Things — Cancelability (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia)

pass_when: A time-consuming operation can be cancelled at once, with no side effects from the cancelled work.
fail_when: No cancel, cancel is not instant, or cancel still applies side effects.

guidelines.title: multilevel undo
guidelines.rule: Let the user reverse a series of actions, not only the last one.

citation.source: Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Doing Things — Multilevel Undo (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia)

pass_when: More than the last action can be reversed.
fail_when: No undo, or only last-action undo.

guidelines.title: command history
guidelines.rule: Keep a visible record of what was done, to what, and when, as the user performs actions.

citation.source: Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Doing Things — Command History (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia)

pass_when: A visible record shows what was done, to what, and when.
fail_when: No visible history of what / to what / when.

guidelines.title: macros
guidelines.rule: Let users compose a sequence of smaller actions into one reusable macro.

citation.source: Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Doing Things — Macros (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia)

pass_when: A sequence of smaller actions can be composed into one reusable macro.
fail_when: Repeated sequences cannot be recorded or reused as a macro.

guidelines.title: short clear sentence case
guidelines.rule: Keep command labels short and clear (NN/g: just enough text, typically up to 2–4 words, drop articles; M3: ideally 1–3 words, sentence case, no wrap).

citation.source: NN/g — UI Copy: UX Guidelines for Command Names and Keyboard Shortcuts; Material 3 — Buttons

pass_when: Label is short and clear: typically 2–4 words (NN/g), articles dropped; and ideally 1–3 words, sentence case, no wrap (M3).
fail_when: Wrapping, padded articles, or a long unclear command name.

guidelines.title: consequent state
guidelines.rule: Command labels describe the state the system will move into, not the current state.
pass_when: The label names the consequent state.
fail_when: The label names the current state instead of the state after the command.

guidelines.title: verbs for actions
guidelines.rule: Lead with a verb (or a specific verb phrase) for commands that initiate an action or submit information; prefer a specific verb over a generic Next.
pass_when: Action/submit commands lead with a verb or specific verb phrase, not a generic Next.
fail_when: Noun-only or generic Next where a specific verb is available.

guidelines.title: adjectives for appearance
guidelines.rule: Use adjectives that name the resulting appearance for commands that change an element’s look or system state (for example Bold, Italic).
pass_when: Look/state-change commands use adjectives that name the resulting appearance (e.g. Bold, Italic).
fail_when: Those commands use unrelated verbs or vague names instead of the appearance adjective.

guidelines.title: avoid vague names
guidelines.rule: Avoid vague, cutesy, or faddish command names; text should be straightforward, descriptive, and accurate.
pass_when: Names are straightforward, descriptive, and accurate.
fail_when: Vague, cutesy, or faddish command names.

guidelines.title: tooltips clarify outcomes
guidelines.rule: When an icon or button initiates an action, include a tooltip that states the outcome without conflicting with the visible label.
pass_when: An action-initiating icon or button has a tooltip that states the outcome and does not conflict with the visible label.
fail_when: No tooltip on that control, or the tooltip conflicts with the visible label.

guidelines.title: limit branded terms
guidelines.rule: Limit branded terms in command text (application name on the app menu and Help is enough); other commands stay nonbranded.
pass_when: App name appears on the app menu and Help as needed; other command text is nonbranded.
fail_when: Brand/product name stuffed into ordinary command labels.

guidelines.title: consistent words
guidelines.rule: Use the same command words in every menu, dialog, or flow for the same action; add a noun when the verb alone is ambiguous.
pass_when: The same action uses the same words across menus, dialogs, and flows; a noun is added when the verb alone is ambiguous.
fail_when: The same action is labeled differently in different places, or an ambiguous verb stands alone.

guidelines.title: explicit verb not ok
guidelines.rule: Do not use generic OK; name the button with the action it commits (and prefer explicit Cancel/Close/Apply text over an unlabeled X).

citation.source: NN/g — UI Copy; NN/g — OK-Cancel or Cancel-OK; NN/g — Cancel vs Close

pass_when: The button names the action it commits; Cancel/Close/Apply are explicit text, not an unlabeled X as the name.
fail_when: Generic OK, or an unlabeled X as the only name for cancel/close/apply.

guidelines.title: ellipsis needs more input
guidelines.rule: Append an ellipsis when the command needs more information or opens another window, view, or app.

citation.source: NN/g — UI Copy; Apple HIG — Buttons

pass_when: Ellipsis is present when more input is required or another window/view/app opens; absent when the action completes immediately.
fail_when: Ellipsis on an immediate-complete command, or no ellipsis when more input / another view is required.

guidelines.title: follow platform ok cancel order
guidelines.rule: Follow the platform convention for OK/Cancel order (Windows: OK first; Apple: OK last; web: the platform of most users).
pass_when: Commit/dismiss order matches the platform (Windows OK first; Apple OK last; web = platform of most users).
fail_when: A third invented sequence, or the opposite of the target platform.

guidelines.title: default not destructive
guidelines.rule: Highlight the common choice as default/primary, but do not assign default or primary to a destructive action (and do not default Yes on a confirmation).

citation.source: NN/g — OK-Cancel or Cancel-OK; Apple HIG — Buttons (don’t assign primary to destructive); NN/g — Confirmation Dialogs (§6 avoid default Yes)

pass_when: The common choice is default/primary; destructive is not default/primary; confirmation does not default Yes.
fail_when: Destructive or confirmation-Yes is the default/primary.

guidelines.title: close saves separate cancel
guidelines.rule: Treat Close as dismiss-and-keep-work and provide a separate Cancel to abandon; when in doubt, save then out.
pass_when: Close (or X-as-close) dismisses and keeps work; a separate Cancel abandons; when in doubt, save then out.
fail_when: One control means both keep and abandon, or Close discards with no separate abandon path.

guidelines.title: serious or undo
guidelines.rule: Before actions with serious consequences (especially those that cannot be undone), use a confirmation dialog, or offer an undo window; never make destruction immediate.

citation.source: NN/g — Confirmation Dialogs (§1); NN/g — Cancel vs Close (ask for confirmation); Vercel Web Interface Guidelines (destructive actions need confirmation modal or undo)

pass_when: Serious / irreversible actions have a confirmation dialog or an undo window; destruction is not immediate.
fail_when: Immediate irreversible destructive commit with neither confirm nor undo.

guidelines.title: not routine
guidelines.rule: Do not use confirmation dialogs for routine actions, or people will stop reading them.
pass_when: Routine actions proceed with no confirmation dialog.
fail_when: Confirmation dialogs on routine actions.

guidelines.title: specific consequences
guidelines.rule: Restate the request with specific, user-centric consequences; do not ask only “Are you sure?”
pass_when: The confirmation restates the request with specific, user-centric consequences.
fail_when: Only “Are you sure?” (or equivalent) with no specific consequence.

guidelines.title: response summarizes outcome
guidelines.rule: Label responses with what will happen (Delete file / Keep file), not Yes/No.
pass_when: Confirmation actions are labeled with the outcome (e.g. Delete file / Keep file).
fail_when: Yes/No (or OK) on the confirmation.

guidelines.title: progressive disclosure
guidelines.rule: Keep confirmation copy short and offer a way to learn more before commit.
pass_when: Confirmation copy is short; extra detail is available before commit.
fail_when: All extra consequence detail dumped on the first screen, or no way to learn more when extra detail exists.

guidelines.title: nonstandard for extreme
guidelines.rule: For particularly dangerous rare operations, require a nonstandard confirm (for example typing a word), reserved so it does not become a new habit.
pass_when: Particularly dangerous rare operations require a nonstandard confirm (e.g. typing a word), used rarely enough that it is not habitual.
fail_when: Extreme danger committed with a single OK click, or nonstandard confirm used so often it is a new habit.

guidelines.title: bypass educational
guidelines.rule: If an educational confirmation is shown for a new non-serious side effect, let the user turn off future repeats.
pass_when: Educational confirmation for a new non-serious side effect offers a way to turn off future repeats.
fail_when: That confirmation has no bypass.

guidelines.title: separate consequential
guidelines.rule: Do not place highly consequential or destructive actions directly next to benign confirmatory options.

citation.source: NN/g — Dangerous UX: Consequential Options Close to Benign Options

pass_when: Highly consequential or destructive actions are not directly next to benign confirmatory options.
fail_when: Destructive sits in the same tight cluster as benign confirm/save.

guidelines.title: redundant visual signals
guidelines.rule: Separate the consequential option with space and redundant visual signals (color, icon, size, alignment), not the label alone.

citation.source: NN/g — Dangerous UX: Consequential Options Close to Benign Options

pass_when: The consequential option is separated with space and more than one of color, icon, size, alignment — not the label alone.
fail_when: Distinction is label-only, or a single non-label cue with no space.

guidelines.title: always visible text label
guidelines.rule: Put a text label next to the icon and keep it visible at all times; do not reveal the label only on hover.
pass_when: Command icons have an always-visible text label next to the icon.
fail_when: Icon-only command, or label only on hover/tooltip.

guidelines.title: distinguishable states
guidelines.rule: Button states (enabled, disabled, hover, focus, pressed) must be visually distinguishable from each other.
pass_when: Enabled, disabled, hover, focus, and pressed are visually distinguishable from each other.
fail_when: Any two of those states look the same.

guidelines.title: loading on button
guidelines.rule: For a slow action, show loading on the button itself (spinner on the control that was pressed).

citation.source: NN/g — Button States: Communicate Interaction; Apple HIG — Buttons (activity indicator when the action does not complete instantly)

pass_when: A slow action shows a spinner/activity indicator on the pressed button itself.
fail_when: No loading on a slow action, or loading only elsewhere (page bar, toast) with none on the control.

guidelines.title: one primary
guidelines.rule: Use one primary (filled) action in the view; other actions use weaker styles.

citation.source: NN/g — Button States: Communicate Interaction; Material 3 — Buttons (filled style ideally for only one action on a page)

pass_when: One primary/filled action in the view; others use weaker styles.
fail_when: Multiple filled/high-emphasis primaries, or no primary/weaker distinction.

guidelines.title: press state
guidelines.rule: Always include a press state on a custom button so the control feels like it accepted input.
pass_when: Custom buttons have a press state that shows the control accepted input.
fail_when: Custom button has no press/active visual.

guidelines.title: style not size
guidelines.rule: Use style, not size, to distinguish the preferred choice among a set of same-role buttons.
pass_when: The preferred same-role button is distinguished by style, not by making it larger.
fail_when: The preferred button is bigger rather than restyled.

guidelines.title: unavailable state
guidelines.rule: Show when a menu item is unavailable (typically dimmed); if every item is unavailable, keep the menu itself openable.
pass_when: Unavailable items are shown as unavailable (typically dimmed); if all items are unavailable, the menu still opens.
fail_when: Unavailable items are omitted with no unavailable state, or the menu cannot be opened when every item is unavailable.

guidelines.title: frequent items first
guidelines.rule: List important or frequently used menu items first (still grouping related commands).
pass_when: Important or frequently used items are listed first, with related commands still grouped.
fail_when: Frequent items are buried, or first-listing scatters related commands with no grouping.
